### ellipsoidTopology2d

Ellipsoid obstacle topology optimization with a volume constraint, using gradients computed by
the adjoint HLBM and the OC optimizer based on the optimality criteria method. The primal flow is computed using HLBM, and porosity
is used as the control variable.
For given in- and outlets at the left and at the right side of a free space and periodic boundary
on the lateral walls, the shape of a ellipsoid has to be found, s.t. either the pressure drop or
dissipation is minimized.
General PDEs-constrained gradient-based optimization problem:

$$
\min_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}} \mathcal{J}(f, \boldsymbol{\alpha}) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \mathcal{G}(f, \boldsymbol{\alpha}) = 0
$$

where $f$ referres to the $state$ and $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ to the $controls$.

#### Primal flow simulation (physical constraint)

---

The primal flow is governed by homogenized Navier–Stokes equations (HNSE):

$$
\mathcal{G}(f,\boldsymbol{\alpha})=
\begin{cases}
\nabla \cdot \mathbf{u} \\
\partial_t \mathbf{u} -\nu \Delta \mathbf{u} + (\mathbf{u} \cdot \nabla) \mathbf{u} + K(\alpha)^{-1} \cdot \mathbf{u} +\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p - \boldsymbol{F} \\
\end{cases}
$$

where $state$ consists of $\mathbf{u}$ and $p$ and $\mathbf{u} \colon \Omega \times I \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^2$ is velocity, $\nu \in \mathbb{R}^+$ is the kinematic viscosity
, $K \colon \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ is the local isotropic permeability, $p \colon \Omega \times I \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{>0}$
is the pressure, $\boldsymbol{F} \in \mathbb{R}^2$ is external force, control variables is porosity $\alpha \colon = d$
and porosity $d \colon \Omega_6 \rightarrow (0,1]$. The physical constraint should fulfill the equation $\mathcal{G}(f,\boldsymbol{\alpha}) = 0$.

##### Geometry and boundary conditions

---

In this section, the free flow around an obstacle is simulated for the 2D cases in the steady laminar
regime, as illustrated in @fig-ellipsoid-opti, is investigated.

![The domain with material number](/examples/optimization/ellipsoidTopology2d/doc/fig/ellipsoidOpti.jpg){#fig-ellipsoid-opti width="60%"}

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RESOLUTION` | `int` | `50` | nodes per Cartesian direction, $N_x$; the elliptic domain is carved out of the square lattice |
| `DOMAIN_X` | `double` | `1.2` | physical length of the entire domain $\Omega$ |
| `DOMAIN_Y` | `double` | `0.4` | physical width of $\Omega$, which is equal to `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` |
| `CENTER_X` | `double` | `0.6` | horizonal coordinate of the design domain $\Omega_6$ center |
| `CENTER_Y` | `double` | `0.2` | vertical coordinate of the $\Omega_6$ center |
| `DESIGN_DOMAIN_X` | `double` | `0.4` | physical length of $\Omega_6$ |
| `DESIGN_DOMAIN_Y` | `double` | `0.2` | physical width of $\Omega_6$ |
| `OBJECTIVE_DOMAIN_X` | `double` | `0.8` | physical length of the dissipation objective domain $\Omega_5$ |
| `OBJECTIVE_DOMAIN_Y` | `double` | `0.4` | physical width of $\Omega_5$ |

Besides that, $\Omega_7$ represents the pressure-in domain and $\Omega_8$ respresents the pressure-out domain.
At the inflow, a Dirichlet velocity boundary condition and at the outlet a Dirichlet pressure boundary condition with $p_{\text{out}} = 0$ is applied. On 
the lateral walls, periodic boundary conditions are applied.

#### Optimization problem setup

---

This topology optimization problem is a classic gradient-based optimization problem constrained by PDEs.
It consists of the following key components.

| Components | Setting | Description |
|---|---|---|
| physical constraint | HLBM | The homogenized Navier–Stokes equations discretized by LBM |
| control variables | porosity $\boldsymbol{d}$ | $\boldsymbol{d} \in (0,1]^n$, $n \in 	\mathbb{N}^+$ is the total number of lattices |
| objective 1 | pressure drop $\Delta p$ | $$\mathcal{J}_1 = \sum_{\boldsymbol{x}_i \in \Omega_7} p_i \Delta x^2 - \sum_{\boldsymbol{x}_i \in \Omega_8} p_i \Delta x^2$$ |
| objective 2 | dissipation $\varepsilon$ | $$\mathcal{J}_2 = \sum_{\boldsymbol{x}_i \in \Omega_5} (\varepsilon^{viscos}_i+\varepsilon^{porous}_i) \Delta x^2$$ |
| gradient computation | AHLBM | The adjoint homogenized LBM, which is commonly used to compute objective gradients with respect to a large number of control variables. |
| optimizer | optimizerOC | optimizer based on the optimality criteria (OC) method, which supports only a single linear constraint |
| control constraint | volume constraint | $$\mathcal{G}_{\text{vol}} = \sum_{\boldsymbol{x}_i \in \Omega_6} (d_i-\bar{d}_{\text{target}}) \Delta x^2$$ |

##### Gradient computation

---

The gradient of the original objective gradient $\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathcal{J}}{\mathrm{d} d_i}$ is 
computed using the AHLBM. But pointwise sensitivities computed on a regular lattice are prone to numerical instabilities that manifest as
checkerboard density patterns [@sigmund1998numerical]. To regularize the problem, we apply the porosity-weighted sensitivity
filter of Sigmund and Bruns and Tortorelli [@sigmund200199line; @bruns2001topology].

$$
\widehat{\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathcal{J}}{\mathrm{d} d_i}} =
\frac{1}{d_i \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_i} w_{ij}}
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_i} w_{ij}\, d_j \,
\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathcal{J}}{\mathrm{d} d_j},
\qquad
w_{ij} = \max\!\left(0,\; r_{\min} - \lVert x_i - x_j\rVert\right)
$$

##### optimizer

---

Following the classical OC method of Bendsøe and Sigmund [@bendsoe2003topology], the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) 
stationarity condition for the
volume constraint requires, at an optimum:

$$
  \widehat{\frac{\mathrm{d} \mathcal{J}_k}{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{d}}} = \lambda \cdot
  \frac{\partial}{\partial \mathbf{d}}\left(\frac{1}{N}\sum_i d_i\right)
  = \frac{\lambda}{N} \quad \text{with} \quad k = \{1,2 \},
$$

where $\lambda$ is the Lagrange multiplier associated with the volume constraint. 
The optimum can be achieved using the iterative update scheme:

$$
  \mathbf{d}^{k+1} =
  \operatorname{clip}\!\left(
    \mathbf{d}^{k} \cdot
    \left(\frac{-\widehat{\mathrm{d} \mathcal{J}}/\mathrm{d} \mathbf{d}}{\lambda}\right)^{\eta},
    \; \mathbf{d}^{k} - m,\;\mathbf{d}^{k} + m
  \right),
$$

Update scheme subsequently clipped to $(0, 1]$. Here $\eta \in (0,1]$ is a damping exponent 
(commonly $\eta = 1/2$) and $m$ is a move limit bounding the per-iteration change in $d$, 
both standard stabilization devices in the OC [@sigmund200199line; @andreassen201188line]. The $\lambda$ can be determined using the bisection
method:

$$
  \overline{d}(\lambda) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_i d_i^{k+1}(\lambda).
$$

The resulting average porosity is monotonically decreasing in $\lambda$, the constraint
$\overline{d}(\lambda) = \bar{d}_{\text{target}}$ admits a unique
solution that is found by bisection [@sigmund200199line; @andreassen201188line]. Because $\lambda$ can span several
orders of magnitude, the bisection is performed on a logarithmic
scale using the geometric mean $\lambda_{\text{mid}} =
\sqrt{\lambda_{\text{lo}}\lambda_{\text{hi}}}$ rather than the
arithmetic mean.

##### Simulation setting

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PHYS_CHAR_LENGTH` | `0.4` | $\text{m}$ |  |
| `REYNOLDS` | `30` |  |  |
| `RESOLUTION` | `50` |  | resolution over design domain width |
| `LATTICE_RELAXATION_TIME` | `0.55` | $\text{s}$ |  |
| `PHYS_CHAR_VELOCITY` | `(0.075, 0.0)` | $\text{m/s}$ | inflow velocity |
| `PHYS_CHAR_DENSITY` | `1.0` | $\text{kg} / \text{m}^3$ |  |
| `PHYS_CHAR_VISCOSITY` | `0.001` | $\text{m}^2 / \text{s}$ |  |
| `TARGET_FLUID_FRACTION` | `0.85` |  | target volume fraction $\bar{d}_\text{target}$ |
| `FILTER_RADIUS` | `0.01` | m | $r_\text{min}$ |
| `OBJECTIVE_TYPE` | `PRESSURE_DROP` |  | pressure drop as the objective function |
